+    ("producer_tp", "consumer_tp", "heads", "mla", "mamba"), _TOPOLOGIES
+)
+def test_every_consumer_head_and_state_slice_is_written_exactly_once(
+    producer_tp, consumer_tp, heads, mla, mamba
+):
+    """Across all producers, each consumer rank receives every global head it
+    holds exactly once, from the producer holding that head, plus every state
+    slice exactly once, and expects as many write_done as producers write."""
+    heads_written: dict[int, list[int]] = {d: [] for d in range(consumer_tp)}
+    slices_written: dict[int, list[int]] = {d: [] for d in range(consumer_tp)}
+    writers: dict[int, set[int]] = {d: set() for d in range(consumer_tp)}
+    advertised: dict[int, set[int]] = {d: set() for d in range(consumer_tp)}
+    for p in range(producer_tp):
+        mapping = compute_write_tp_mapping(
+            p, producer_tp, consumer_tp, heads, mla, mamba
+        )
+        p_heads = _rank_heads(p, producer_tp, 1 if mla else heads)
+        for t in mapping.targets:
+            d_heads = _rank_heads(t.tp_rank, consumer_tp, 1 if mla else heads)
+            for i in range(t.num_heads):
+                # The global head sent is the global head it lands on.
+                assert p_heads.start + t.local_head + i == (
+                    d_heads.start + t.remote_head + i
+                )
+                heads_written[t.tp_rank].append(d_heads.start + t.remote_head + i)
+            if mamba:
+                assert t.local_slices == 1 or t.remote_slices == 1
+                slices_written[t.tp_rank].append(t.remote_slice)
+            writers[t.tp_rank].add(p)
+            advertised[t.tp_rank].add(t.num_writers)
+
+    for d in range(consumer_tp):
+        d_heads = _rank_heads(d, consumer_tp, 1 if mla else heads)
+        assert sorted(heads_written[d]) == list(d_heads)
+        if mamba:
+            ratio = max(1, producer_tp // consumer_tp)
+            assert sorted(slices_written[d]) == list(range(ratio))
+        assert advertised[d] == {len(writers[d])}
+

+def _view(buffer: torch.Tensor, spec, num_blocks, layout) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """A byte view [B, H, N, C] of ``buffer`` laid out as ``layout``."""
+    strides = compute_layout_strides(spec, num_blocks, 1, layout)[1:]
+    shape = (num_blocks, spec.num_heads, spec.num_states, spec.state_content_size_bytes)
+    return torch.as_strided(buffer, shape, strides)
+
+
+def _spec(num_kv_heads: int) -> FullAttentionSpec:
+    return FullAttentionSpec(
+        block_size=4, num_kv_heads=num_kv_heads, head_size=2, dtype=torch.bfloat16
+    )
+
+
+def _apply(offsets, src: torch.Tensor, dst: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+    for local, remote, size in zip(*offsets):
+        dst[remote : remote + size] = src[local : local + size]
+
+
+_LAYOUTS = (KVCacheLayout.LBNHC, KVCacheLayout.LBHNC, KVCacheLayout.LHBNC)
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("local_layout", "remote_layout"), list(itertools.product(_LAYOUTS, _LAYOUTS))
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("producer_tp", "consumer_tp"), [(1, 2), (2, 4), (2, 1)])
+def test_head_slices_land_byte_exact(
+    local_layout, remote_layout, producer_tp, consumer_tp
+):
+    total_heads, num_blocks = 4, 3
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    full = torch.randint(0, 255, (num_blocks, total_heads, 4, 8), dtype=torch.uint8)
+    local_blocks, remote_blocks = [0, 2], [2, 1]
+    expected = {}
+    received = {}
+    consumers = {}
+    for d in range(consumer_tp):
+        spec = _spec(total_heads // consumer_tp)
+        buffer = torch.zeros(spec.page_size_bytes * num_blocks, dtype=torch.uint8)
+        consumers[d] = (buffer, _view(buffer, spec, num_blocks, remote_layout), spec)
+    for p in range(producer_tp):
+        spec = _spec(total_heads // producer_tp)
+        buffer = torch.zeros(spec.page_size_bytes * num_blocks, dtype=torch.uint8)
+        view = _view(buffer, spec, num_blocks, local_layout)
+        view.copy_(full[:, _rank_heads(p, producer_tp, total_heads)])
+        local = get_layer_head_layout("l", view, {"l": spec})
+        mapping = compute_write_tp_mapping(
+            p, producer_tp, consumer_tp, total_heads, False, False
+        )
+        for t in mapping.targets:
+            remote_buffer, remote_view, remote_spec = consumers[t.tp_rank]
+            remote = get_layer_head_layout("l", remote_view, {"l": remote_spec})
+            offsets = compute_head_slice_offsets(
+                local,
+                HeadLayout.from_wire(remote.to_wire()),
+                local_blocks,
+                remote_blocks,
+                t.local_head,
+                t.remote_head,
+                t.num_heads,
+            )
+            _apply(offsets, buffer, remote_buffer)
+    for d, (_, remote_view, _) in consumers.items():
+        d_heads = _rank_heads(d, consumer_tp, total_heads)
+        expected[d] = full[local_blocks][:, d_heads]
+        received[d] = remote_view[remote_blocks]
+        assert torch.equal(received[d], expected[d])
+        # Blocks nobody wrote stay untouched.
+        assert not remote_view[0].any()

+def _mamba_layout(proj, ssm, conv_stride, ssm_stride):
+    return MambaStateLayout(conv_stride, ssm_stride, ssm, tuple(proj))

+def _fill(layout: MambaStateLayout, slots, num_slots, seed):
+    torch.manual_seed(seed)
+    conv = torch.zeros(layout.conv_slot_stride * num_slots, dtype=torch.uint8)
+    ssm = torch.zeros(layout.ssm_slot_stride * num_slots, dtype=torch.uint8)
+    for slot in slots:
+        base = slot * layout.conv_slot_stride
+        n = sum(layout.conv_proj_bytes)
+        conv[base : base + n] = torch.randint(1, 255, (n,), dtype=torch.uint8)
+        base = slot * layout.ssm_slot_stride
+        ssm[base : base + layout.ssm_bytes] = torch.randint(
+            1, 255, (layout.ssm_bytes,), dtype=torch.uint8
+        )
+    return conv, ssm

+def _move_state(offsets, src, dst):
+    local, remote, sizes, n_conv = offsets
+    _apply((local[:n_conv], remote[:n_conv], sizes[:n_conv]), src[0], dst[0])
+    _apply((local[n_conv:], remote[n_conv:], sizes[n_conv:]), src[1], dst[1])

+def test_mamba_state_fans_out_and_gathers_back(replicated_bc):
+    # x, B, C sub-projections and the SSM state, TP1 vs TP2 pages.
+    big = _mamba_layout((8, 4, 4), 16, conv_stride=40, ssm_stride=24)
+    small = _mamba_layout(
+        (4, 4, 4) if replicated_bc else (4, 2, 2), 8, conv_stride=20, ssm_stride=12
+    )
+    full = _fill(big, [1], 3, seed=0)
+
+    # Fan-out: one TP1 producer slot 1 -> slot 2 of both TP2 consumers.
+    shards = []
+    for j in range(2):
+        shard = (
+            torch.zeros(20 * 3, dtype=torch.uint8),
+            torch.zeros(12 * 3, dtype=torch.uint8),
+        )
+        offsets = compute_mamba_slice_offsets(big, small, [1], [2], j, 2, 0, 1)
+        _move_state(offsets, full, shard)
+        shards.append(shard)
+    for j, (conv, ssm) in enumerate(shards):
+        x = full[0][40:48].view(2, 4)[j]
+        b = full[0][48:52] if replicated_bc else full[0][48:52].view(2, 2)[j]
+        c = full[0][52:56] if replicated_bc else full[0][52:56].view(2, 2)[j]
+        assert torch.equal(conv[40 : 40 + 4], x)
+        assert torch.equal(conv[44 : 44 + b.numel()], b)
+        assert torch.equal(conv[44 + b.numel() : 44 + 2 * b.numel()], c)
+        assert torch.equal(ssm[24 : 24 + 8], full[1][24:40].view(2, 8)[j])
+
+    # Fan-in: both TP2 producers write their slot 2 back into one TP1 slot 0.

+        torch.zeros(24 * 3, dtype=torch.uint8),

+        _move_state(offsets, shard, gathered)

+    assert torch.equal(gathered[1][:16], full[1][24:40])

+class HeadLayout(NamedTuple):
+    """Byte addressing of one attention layer's KV heads in its region.
+
+    Offsets are relative to the layer's registered region. ``plane_offsets``
+    holds the start of the K and V planes when they are stored apart, or
+    ``(0,)`` when K and V are packed into each head's content.
+    """

+    num_heads: int
+    num_tokens: int
+    head_bytes: int
+    block_stride: int
+    head_stride: int
+    token_stride: int
+    plane_offsets: tuple[int, ...]
+
+    @property
+    def is_dense(self) -> bool:
+        """Each block plane is one contiguous run of all its heads and tokens."""
+        hb = self.head_bytes
+        return (
+            self.head_stride == hb and self.token_stride == self.num_heads * hb
+        ) or (self.token_stride == hb and self.head_stride == self.num_tokens * hb)
+
+    def to_wire(self) -> list[int]:
+        return [*self[:6], *self.plane_offsets]
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_wire(cls, values: list[int]) -> "HeadLayout":
+        heads, tokens, head_bytes, block_stride, head_stride, token_stride, *planes = (
+            values
+        )
+        return cls(
+            heads,
+            tokens,
+            head_bytes,
+            block_stride,
+            head_stride,
+            token_stride,
+            tuple(planes),
+        )

+    if spec is None:
+        raise ValueError(f"Missing KV cache spec for layer {layer_name}")
+    shape = kv_cache.shape
+    stride = kv_cache.stride()
+    element_size = kv_cache.element_size()
+    if not is_mla_cache_layer(layer_to_spec, layer_name) and len(shape) == 5:
+        if shape[0] == 2:
+            plane_axis, block_axis = 0, 1
+        elif shape[1] == 2:
+            plane_axis, block_axis = 1, 0
+        else:
+            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported K/V cache shape {tuple(shape)}")
+        if shape[2] == spec.block_size:
+            token_axis, head_axis = 2, 3
+        elif shape[3] == spec.block_size:
+            token_axis, head_axis = 3, 2

+            raise ValueError(
+                f"MoRIIO cannot slice KV heads of layer {layer_name}: kernel "
+                f"blocks {tuple(shape)} split the {spec.block_size}-token block"

+            num_tokens=shape[token_axis],

+            block_stride=stride[block_axis] * element_size,
+            head_stride=stride[head_axis] * element_size,
+            token_stride=stride[token_axis] * element_size,

+    if layout.token_stride == hb and layout.head_stride == layout.num_tokens * hb:
+        # Head-major with packed tokens: the heads are one contiguous run.
+        return "block", [
+            (first_head * layout.head_stride, num_heads * layout.head_stride)
+        ]
+    if layout.token_stride == hb:
+        # Head-major: one run of all tokens per head.
+        return "head", [(h * layout.head_stride, layout.num_tokens * hb) for h in heads]
+    if layout.head_stride == hb:
+        # Token-major: one run of adjacent heads per token.
+        return "token", [
+            (t * layout.token_stride + first_head * hb, num_heads * hb)
+            for t in range(layout.num_tokens)
+        ]
+    return "element", _element_runs(layout, first_head, num_heads)
+
+
+def _element_runs(
+    layout: HeadLayout, first_head: int, num_heads: int
+) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
+    """One run per (token, head), ordered token-major."""
+    return [
+        (t * layout.token_stride + h * layout.head_stride, layout.head_bytes)
+        for t in range(layout.num_tokens)
+        for h in range(first_head, first_head + num_heads)
+    ]
+
+
+def compute_head_slice_offsets(
+    local: HeadLayout,
+    remote: HeadLayout,
+    local_block_ids: list[int],
+    remote_block_ids: list[int],
+    local_head: int,
+    remote_head: int,
+    num_heads: int,
+    merge_fn: Callable[
+        [list[int], list[int], list[int]], tuple[list[int], list[int], list[int]]
+    ] = merge_contiguous_offsets,
+) -> tuple[list[int], list[int], list[int]]:
+    """Offsets copying ``num_heads`` heads of each local block into a remote one.
+
+    Local heads ``[local_head, local_head + num_heads)`` land on remote heads
+    ``[remote_head, remote_head + num_heads)``; every other remote head is
+    left for the producer rank that holds it.
+    """
+    if (
+        local.num_tokens != remote.num_tokens
+        or local.head_bytes != remote.head_bytes
+        or len(local.plane_offsets) != len(remote.plane_offsets)
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "MoRIIO head slicing needs the same block size, head size and K/V "
+            f"planes on both sides, got local {local} and remote {remote}"
+        )
+    if not (
+        local_head >= 0
+        and local_head + num_heads <= local.num_heads
+        and remote_head >= 0
+        and remote_head + num_heads <= remote.num_heads
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Head slice local [{local_head}, {local_head + num_heads}) / remote "
+            f"[{remote_head}, {remote_head + num_heads}) is outside "
+            f"{local.num_heads} / {remote.num_heads} heads"
+        )
+    if len(local_block_ids) > len(remote_block_ids):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "local_block_ids longer than remote_block_ids: "
+            f"{len(local_block_ids)} > {len(remote_block_ids)}"
+        )
+    local_kind, local_runs = _head_runs(local, local_head, num_heads)
+    remote_kind, remote_runs = _head_runs(remote, remote_head, num_heads)
+    if local_kind != remote_kind:
+        # The two sides order heads and tokens differently: pair single
+        # (token, head) runs, which merge_fn coalesces where both are adjacent.
+        local_runs = _element_runs(local, local_head, num_heads)
+        remote_runs = _element_runs(remote, remote_head, num_heads)
+
+    offset_local: list[int] = []
+    offset_remote: list[int] = []
+    sizes: list[int] = []
+    for local_plane, remote_plane in zip(local.plane_offsets, remote.plane_offsets):
+        for lb, rb in zip(local_block_ids, remote_block_ids):
+            local_base = local_plane + lb * local.block_stride
+            remote_base = remote_plane + rb * remote.block_stride
+            for (local_off, size), (remote_off, _) in zip(local_runs, remote_runs):
+                offset_local.append(local_base + local_off)
+                offset_remote.append(remote_base + remote_off)
+                sizes.append(size)
+    return merge_fn(offset_local, offset_remote, sizes)
+
+
+class MambaStateLayout(NamedTuple):
+    """Byte addressing of one mamba layer's per-slot conv and SSM state."""
+
+    conv_slot_stride: int
+    ssm_slot_stride: int
+    ssm_bytes: int
+    conv_proj_bytes: tuple[int, ...]
+
+    def to_wire(self) -> list[int]:
+        return [*self[:3], *self.conv_proj_bytes]
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_wire(cls, values: list[int]) -> "MambaStateLayout":
+        conv_slot_stride, ssm_slot_stride, ssm_bytes, *conv_proj_bytes = values
+        return cls(conv_slot_stride, ssm_slot_stride, ssm_bytes, tuple(conv_proj_bytes))
+
+
+def get_mamba_state_layout(
+    conv: torch.Tensor, ssm: torch.Tensor, split_info: MambaConvSplitInfo
+) -> MambaStateLayout:
+    geom = get_mamba_transfer_geometry(conv, ssm)
+    return MambaStateLayout(
+        conv_slot_stride=geom.conv_slot_stride * geom.conv_element_size,
+        ssm_slot_stride=geom.ssm_slot_stride * geom.ssm_element_size,
+        ssm_bytes=geom.ssm_slot_bytes,
+        conv_proj_bytes=split_info.proj_bytes,
+    )
+
+
+def _state_slice(
+    local_bytes: int,
+    remote_bytes: int,
+    local_slice: int,
+    local_slices: int,
+    remote_slice: int,
+    remote_slices: int,
+) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
+    """(local offset, remote offset, size) of the bytes one target receives."""
+    if local_bytes == remote_bytes:
+        # Equal TP, or a part replicated on both sides (e.g. Mamba2 B/C with
+        # fewer groups than ranks): copy it whole.
+        return 0, 0, local_bytes
+    if local_slices > 1 and local_bytes == local_slices * remote_bytes:
+        return local_slice * remote_bytes, 0, remote_bytes
+    if remote_slices > 1 and remote_bytes == remote_slices * local_bytes:
+        return 0, remote_slice * local_bytes, local_bytes
+    raise ValueError(
+        f"MoRIIO cannot map {local_bytes} local state bytes onto {remote_bytes} "
+        f"remote bytes for slice {local_slice}/{local_slices} -> "
+        f"{remote_slice}/{remote_slices}"
+    )
+
+
+def compute_mamba_slice_offsets(
+    local: MambaStateLayout,
+    remote: MambaStateLayout,
+    local_slots: list[int],
+    remote_slots: list[int],
+    local_slice: int,
+    local_slices: int,
+    remote_slice: int,
+    remote_slices: int,
+) -> tuple[list[int], list[int], list[int], int]:
+    """(local, remote, sizes, n_conv) moving one target's share of the state.
+
+    Entries ``[:n_conv]`` address the conv region; the rest the SSM region.
+    Each conv sub-projection and the SSM state are sharded across TP ranks
+    independently, so each is sliced or gathered on its own.
+    """
+    if len(local_slots) != len(remote_slots):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "local and remote mamba slot counts must match: "
+            f"{len(local_slots)} != {len(remote_slots)}"
+        )
+    if len(local.conv_proj_bytes) != len(remote.conv_proj_bytes):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "local and remote conv states have different sub-projections: "
+            f"{local.conv_proj_bytes} vs {remote.conv_proj_bytes}"
+        )
+    slices = (local_slice, local_slices, remote_slice, remote_slices)
+    conv_parts = []
+    local_base = remote_base = 0
+    for local_bytes, remote_bytes in zip(local.conv_proj_bytes, remote.conv_proj_bytes):
+        local_off, remote_off, size = _state_slice(local_bytes, remote_bytes, *slices)
+        conv_parts.append((local_base + local_off, remote_base + remote_off, size))
+        local_base += local_bytes
+        remote_base += remote_bytes
+    ssm_local, ssm_remote, ssm_size = _state_slice(
+        local.ssm_bytes, remote.ssm_bytes, *slices
+    )
+
+    local_offs: list[int] = []
+    remote_offs: list[int] = []
+    sizes: list[int] = []
+    for ls, rs in zip(local_slots, remote_slots):
+        for local_off, remote_off, size in conv_parts:
+            local_offs.append(ls * local.conv_slot_stride + local_off)
+            remote_offs.append(rs * remote.conv_slot_stride + remote_off)
+            sizes.append(size)
+    n_conv = len(sizes)
+    for ls, rs in zip(local_slots, remote_slots):
+        local_offs.append(ls * local.ssm_slot_stride + ssm_local)
+        remote_offs.append(rs * remote.ssm_slot_stride + ssm_remote)
+        sizes.append(ssm_size)
+    return local_offs, remote_offs, sizes, n_conv

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Producer-to-consumer TP mapping for MoRIIO WRITE transfers.
+
+In WRITE mode every prefill (producer) rank pushes its own shard of the KV
+cache and recurrent state into the decode (consumer) ranks that need it:
+
+* consumer TP > producer TP (fan-out): producer rank ``p`` feeds consumer ranks
+  ``p * r .. p * r + r - 1``. MLA latents and replicated KV heads are copied
+  whole to each of them; split KV heads and mamba state are sliced, and each
+  consumer gets its slice.
+* producer TP > consumer TP (fan-in): consumer rank ``d`` is fed by producer
+  ranks ``d * r .. d * r + r - 1``. Split KV heads and mamba state are
+  gathered: each producer writes its shard at its offset inside the consumer's
+  block. Copies that would be identical (MLA, replicated heads) are written by
+  one producer only.
+
+Heads follow vLLM's sharding: with ``tp_size <= num_kv_heads`` rank ``i`` holds
+heads ``[i * n, (i + 1) * n)`` with ``n = num_kv_heads // tp_size``; with more
+ranks than heads every rank holds the single head ``i * num_kv_heads //
+tp_size``.
+"""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from functools import cache
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class WriteTarget:
+    """What one producer rank writes into one consumer rank."""
+
+    tp_rank: int
+    # Attention: copy ``num_heads`` heads starting at ``local_head`` of the
+    # producer block into the consumer block starting at ``remote_head``.
+    # ``num_heads == 0`` means another producer writes this identical copy.
+    local_head: int
+    remote_head: int
+    num_heads: int
+    # Mamba state: the producer's state is ``local_slices`` equal slices of
+    # which ``local_slice`` is sent; it lands in slot ``remote_slice`` of the
+    # consumer's ``remote_slices`` equal slices.
+    local_slice: int
+    local_slices: int
+    remote_slice: int
+    remote_slices: int
+    # Producer ranks writing into this consumer rank, each sending one
+    # ``write_done``; the consumer has its KV once all of them arrived.
+    num_writers: int
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class MoRIIOWriteTPMapping:
+    """Write targets of one producer rank for one consumer engine."""
+
+    producer_tp_size: int
+    consumer_tp_size: int
+    local_num_heads: int
+    remote_num_heads: int
+    # Consumer ranks this producer writes to. Empty when another producer
+    # writes everything this one holds (MLA or replicated heads, fan-in).
+    targets: tuple[WriteTarget, ...]
+
+    @property
+    def target_tp_ranks(self) -> tuple[int, ...]:
+        return tuple(target.tp_rank for target in self.targets)
+
+    def copies_whole_block(self, target: WriteTarget) -> bool:
+        """The consumer block is a byte copy of the producer block."""
+        return target.num_heads == self.local_num_heads == self.remote_num_heads
+
+
+def _rank_heads(tp_rank: int, tp_size: int, total_num_kv_heads: int) -> range:
+    if tp_size <= total_num_kv_heads:
+        per_rank = total_num_kv_heads // tp_size
+        return range(tp_rank * per_rank, (tp_rank + 1) * per_rank)
+    head = tp_rank * total_num_kv_heads // tp_size
+    return range(head, head + 1)
+
+
+def validate_write_tp_topology(
+    producer_tp_size: int,
+    consumer_tp_size: int,
+    total_num_kv_heads: int,
+    is_mla: bool,
+) -> None:
+    """Reject TP pairs that the WRITE mapping cannot express."""
+    if producer_tp_size <= 0 or consumer_tp_size <= 0:
+        raise ValueError("TP sizes must be positive")
+    larger = max(producer_tp_size, consumer_tp_size)
+    smaller = min(producer_tp_size, consumer_tp_size)
+    if larger % smaller != 0:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "MoRIIO WRITE needs one TP size to be a multiple of the other, got "
+            f"producer tp_size={producer_tp_size}, consumer "
+            f"tp_size={consumer_tp_size}"
+        )
+    if is_mla or producer_tp_size == consumer_tp_size:
+        return
+    if total_num_kv_heads <= 0:
+        raise ValueError("total_num_kv_heads must be positive")
+    for tp_size in (producer_tp_size, consumer_tp_size):
+        if (tp_size <= total_num_kv_heads and total_num_kv_heads % tp_size) or (
+            tp_size > total_num_kv_heads and tp_size % total_num_kv_heads
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"MoRIIO WRITE cannot shard {total_num_kv_heads} KV heads over "
+                f"tp_size={tp_size}"
+            )
+
+
+def _producer_targets(
+    producer_tp_rank: int,
+    producer_tp_size: int,
+    consumer_tp_size: int,
+    num_heads: int,
+    has_mamba: bool,
+) -> list[WriteTarget]:
+    local_heads = _rank_heads(producer_tp_rank, producer_tp_size, num_heads)
+    if consumer_tp_size >= producer_tp_size:
+        ratio = consumer_tp_size // producer_tp_size
+        targets = []
+        for j in range(ratio):
+            tp_rank = producer_tp_rank * ratio + j
+            remote_heads = _rank_heads(tp_rank, consumer_tp_size, num_heads)
+            targets.append(
+                WriteTarget(
+                    tp_rank=tp_rank,
+                    local_head=remote_heads.start - local_heads.start,
+                    remote_head=0,
+                    num_heads=len(remote_heads),
+                    local_slice=j,
+                    local_slices=ratio,
+                    remote_slice=0,
+                    remote_slices=1,
+                    num_writers=1,
+                )
+            )
+        return targets
+
+    ratio = producer_tp_size // consumer_tp_size
+    tp_rank = producer_tp_rank // ratio
+    remote_heads = _rank_heads(tp_rank, consumer_tp_size, num_heads)
+    # The first producer holding a head writes it; the others hold an
+    # identical copy and skip the attention write.
+    group = range(tp_rank * ratio, (tp_rank + 1) * ratio)
+    first_holder = next(
+        p
+        for p in group
+        if _rank_heads(p, producer_tp_size, num_heads).start == local_heads.start
+    )
+    writes_attention = first_holder == producer_tp_rank
+    if not writes_attention and not has_mamba:
+        return []
+    writers = sum(
+        1
+        for p in group
+        if has_mamba
+        or _rank_heads(p, producer_tp_size, num_heads).start
+        not in {
+            _rank_heads(q, producer_tp_size, num_heads).start
+            for q in range(group.start, p)
+        }
+    )
+    return [
+        WriteTarget(
+            tp_rank=tp_rank,
+            local_head=0,
+            remote_head=local_heads.start - remote_heads.start,
+            num_heads=len(local_heads) if writes_attention else 0,
+            local_slice=0,
+            local_slices=1,
+            remote_slice=producer_tp_rank % ratio,
+            remote_slices=ratio,
+            num_writers=writers,
+        )
+    ]
+
+
+@cache
+def compute_write_tp_mapping(
+    producer_tp_rank: int,
+    producer_tp_size: int,
+    consumer_tp_size: int,
+    total_num_kv_heads: int,
+    is_mla: bool,
+    has_mamba: bool,
+) -> MoRIIOWriteTPMapping:
+    """Map one producer rank onto the consumer ranks it writes."""
+    validate_write_tp_topology(
+        producer_tp_size, consumer_tp_size, total_num_kv_heads, is_mla
+    )
+    if not 0 <= producer_tp_rank < producer_tp_size:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"producer_tp_rank {producer_tp_rank} must be in [0, {producer_tp_size})"
+        )
+    num_heads = 1 if is_mla else total_num_kv_heads
+    first_remote_rank = producer_tp_rank * consumer_tp_size // producer_tp_size
+    return MoRIIOWriteTPMapping(
+        producer_tp_size=producer_tp_size,
+        consumer_tp_size=consumer_tp_size,
+        local_num_heads=len(_rank_heads(producer_tp_rank, producer_tp_size, num_heads)),
+        remote_num_heads=len(
+            _rank_heads(first_remote_rank, consumer_tp_size, num_heads)
+        ),
+        targets=tuple(
+            _producer_targets(
+                producer_tp_rank,
+                producer_tp_size,
+                consumer_tp_size,
+                num_heads,
+                has_mamba,
+            )
+        ),
+    )

+            0.75 * subnormal,
+            1.5 * subnormal,
+            info.tiny - subnormal / 2,
+        ]
+    )
+    key = torch.cat((values, -values)).repeat(2).reshape(1, 1, 32)
+    key_cache = torch.empty((1, 1, 32, 32), dtype=torch.uint8)
+    value_cache = torch.empty_like(key_cache)
+    cpu_attn_reshape_and_cache(
+        key,
+        key,
+        key_cache,
+        value_cache,
+        torch.tensor([0]),
+        "vec",
+        kv_cache_dtype=kv_cache_dtype,
+    )
+    expected = key.to(fp8_dtype).view(torch.uint8).flatten()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(key_cache[0, 0, :, 0], expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(value_cache[0, 0, 0], expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
 @pytest.mark.parametrize("kv_cache_dtype", ["auto", "fp8_e4m3", "fp8_e5m2"])
 @pytest.mark.parametrize("seq_lens", SEQ_LENS)
 @pytest.mark.parametrize("num_heads", NUM_HEADS)

+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.auto_gptq import AutoGPTQConfig
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.moe_wna16 import (

+)

+class INCARKWNA16MoEMethod(MoeWNA16Method):
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        quant_config: MoeWNA16Config,
+        moe: FusedMoEConfig,
+    ) -> None:
+        if quant_config.weight_bits != 4 or quant_config.has_zp:
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                "ARK WNA16 MoE only supports symmetric int4 W4A16 for now."
+            )
+
+        super().__init__(quant_config, moe)
+
+        from .inc_ark_ops import get_ark_state
+
+        is_available, error_str, ark, _ = get_ark_state()
+        xpu_lib = getattr(ark, "xpu_lib", None) if ark is not None else None
+        has_moe_kernel = (
+            is_available
+            and ark is not None
+            and hasattr(ark, "MoeSymmetricGemm")
+            and xpu_lib is not None
+        )
+        if not has_moe_kernel:
+            reason = error_str or "ARK MoE kernels are unavailable."
+            raise ImportError(f"Failed to initialize ARK WNA16 MoE. {reason}")
+
+        assert ark is not None
+        self.ark = ark
+        self.remap_hidden_states_op = None
+        self.moe_gather_op = None
+        self.local_num_experts: int | None = None
+        self.global_num_experts: int | None = None
+        self.expert_map: torch.Tensor | None = None
+        self.rows_per_expert: torch.Tensor | None = None
+        self.unpermuted_row_to_permuted_row: torch.Tensor | None = None
+        self.router_weight_ones: torch.Tensor | None = None
+        self.router_weights_fn = self._keep_router_weights
+        self.activation = None
+        self.activation_config = ApplyMoEActivationConfig.from_configs(
+            moe,
+            FusedMoEQuantConfig.make(),
+        )
+        self.inter_size: int = 0
+        self.inter_size_scale: int = 1
+        self.w13_moe = None
+        self.w2_moe = None
+
+        logger.info_once("Using ARK XPU WNA16 MoE kernel.")
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer) -> None:
+        # ARK int4 MoE with asym=False expects signed nibbles [-8, 7].
+        # Loaded GPTQ weights are unsigned nibbles [0, 15], so flip the sign
+        # bit of each nibble, equivalent to q - 8 in 4-bit two's-complement.
+        w13_qweight = torch.bitwise_xor(
+            layer.w13_qweight.detach().contiguous(),
+            0x88,
+        )
+        w2_qweight = torch.bitwise_xor(
+            layer.w2_qweight.detach().contiguous(),
+            0x88,
+        )
+
+        replace_parameter(layer, "w13_qweight", w13_qweight)
+        replace_parameter(layer, "w2_qweight", w2_qweight)
+        replace_parameter(layer, "w13_scales", layer.w13_scales.detach().contiguous())
+        replace_parameter(layer, "w2_scales", layer.w2_scales.detach().contiguous())
+
+        layer.w13_weight = layer.w13_qweight
+        layer.w2_weight = layer.w2_qweight
+        num_local_experts = layer.w13_weight.shape[0]
+        self.local_num_experts = num_local_experts
+        self.global_num_experts = layer.global_num_experts
+        self.expert_map = layer.expert_map
+        self.rows_per_expert = torch.empty(
+            (num_local_experts,),
+            dtype=torch.int32,
+            device=layer.w13_weight.device,

+                gemm1_beta=getattr(layer, "swiglu_beta", None),
+                gemm1_clamp_limit=getattr(layer, "swiglu_limit", None),

+    def _get_rows_per_expert(
+        self,
+        local_num_experts: int,
+        device: torch.device,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        rows_per_expert = self.rows_per_expert
+        if rows_per_expert is None or rows_per_expert.device != device:
+            rows_per_expert = torch.empty(
+                (local_num_experts,),
+                dtype=torch.int32,

+    def _get_unpermuted_row_to_permuted_row(
+        self,

+        mapping = self.unpermuted_row_to_permuted_row

+        self,

+        dtype: torch.dtype,

+            router_weight_ones is None
+            or router_weight_ones.device != device
+            or router_weight_ones.dtype != dtype
+            or router_weight_ones.shape[0] < num_rows
+            or router_weight_ones.shape[1] != topk

+        topk: int,

+        topk_weights: torch.Tensor,
+        num_rows: int,
+        topk: int,

+            num_rows,
+            topk,

+            topk_weights,

+        assert self.w13_moe is not None
+        assert self.w2_moe is not None

+            topk_ids=topk_ids,
+            total_experts_num=self.global_num_experts,
+            local_experts_num=self.local_num_experts,
+        )

+            remapped_hidden_states,
+            rows_per_expert,
+            phase="auto",
+        )
+
+        act_output = gemm1_output.new_empty(
+            (gemm1_output.shape[0], self.inter_size * self.inter_size_scale)
+        )
+
+        apply_moe_activation(
+            self.activation,
+            act_output,
+            gemm1_output,
+            activation_config=self.activation_config,
+        )
+
+        gemm2_output = self.w2_moe.apply(
+            act_output,
+            rows_per_expert,
+            phase="auto",
+        )
+
+        self.moe_gather_op(

+            gemm2_output,
+            gather_topk_weights,
+            unpermuted_row_to_permuted_row,

+        raise NotImplementedError(

+        from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe import (
+            UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod,

+    def _build_gptq_method(self, layer: torch.nn.Module):

+            check_moe_marlin_supports_layer,

+

+            group_size,
+        )
+
+        if use_marlin:

+                AutoAWQConfig(
+                    weight_bits=self.layer_config.bits,
+                    group_size=group_size,
+                    zero_point=not self.layer_config.sym,
+                    lm_head_quantized=False,
+                    modules_to_not_convert=[],
+                    full_config={},

+        moe_config = MoeWNA16Config.from_config(

+                "zero_point": not self.layer_config.sym,

+        )

+MODEL_NAME = "athrael-soju/ColUltraVBERT"
+DTYPE = "bfloat16"

+IMAGE_SEQ_LEN = 64
+EMBEDDING_DIM = 768
+LONGEST_EDGE = 3072
+TILE_SIZE = 512
+MAX_IMAGE_TILES = 27

+
+def page_grid(width: int, height: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    edge = get_capped_longest_edge(
+        height, width, LONGEST_EDGE, TILE_SIZE, MAX_IMAGE_TILES
+    )
+    processor = Idefics3ImageProcessor(
+        size={"longest_edge": LONGEST_EDGE},
+        max_image_size={"longest_edge": TILE_SIZE},
+    )
+    _, rows, cols = processor.get_number_of_image_patches(
+        height, width, {"size": {"longest_edge": edge}}
+    )
+    return rows, cols
+
+
+# Grids from the checkpoint's own UltraVBertImageProcessor.
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("width", "height", "grid"),
+    [
+        (1700, 2200, (5, 4)),
+        (2200, 1700, (4, 5)),
+        (2000, 2000, (5, 5)),
+        (4000, 1000, (2, 6)),
+        (1000, 4000, (6, 2)),
+        (300, 200, (4, 6)),
+        (3000, 2400, (4, 5)),
+    ],
+)
+def test_colultravbert_tile_cap(width, height, grid):
+    assert page_grid(width, height) == grid
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def colultravbert_model(vllm_runner):
+    with vllm_runner(
+        MODEL_NAME,
+        runner="pooling",
+        dtype=DTYPE,
+        max_model_len=2048,
+        enforce_eager=True,
+    ) as vllm_model:
+        yield vllm_model
+
+
+def test_colultravbert_text_token_embed(colultravbert_model):
+    outputs = colultravbert_model.token_embed(["What is machine learning?"])
+
+    assert len(outputs) == 1
+    emb = torch.tensor(outputs[0])
+    assert emb.dim() == 2
+    assert emb.shape[1] == EMBEDDING_DIM
+    assert emb.shape[0] > 1
+
+
+def test_colultravbert_text_relevance_ordering(colultravbert_model):
+    query = "What is machine learning?"

+        "The weather in Paris is mild in spring.",
+    ]

+def test_colultravbert_text_late_interaction(colultravbert_model):
+    query = "What is the capital of France?"
+    doc = "The capital of France is Paris."

+    q_emb = torch.tensor(q_out[0])

+    rows, cols = page_grid(*image.size)

+class UltraBertAttention(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: UltraBertConfig,
+        layer_id: int,
+        quant_config: QuantizationConfig | None = None,
+        prefix: str = "",
+    ):
+        super().__init__()
+        tp_size = get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size()
+        self.total_num_heads = config.num_attention_heads
+        self.total_num_kv_heads = config.num_key_value_heads
+        assert self.total_num_heads % tp_size == 0
+        self.num_heads = self.total_num_heads // tp_size
+        self.num_kv_heads = max(1, self.total_num_kv_heads // tp_size)
+        self.head_dim = config.head_dim
+        self.q_size = self.num_heads * self.head_dim
+        self.kv_size = self.num_kv_heads * self.head_dim
+
+        self.qkv_proj = QKVParallelLinear(
+            config.hidden_size,
+            self.head_dim,
+            self.total_num_heads,
+            self.total_num_kv_heads,
+            bias=config.attention_bias,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.qkv_proj",
+        )
+        self.o_proj = RowParallelLinear(
+            self.total_num_heads * self.head_dim,
+            config.hidden_size,
+            bias=config.attention_bias,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.o_proj",
+        )
+
+        layer_type = config.layer_types[layer_id]
+        self.rotary_emb = get_rope(
+            self.head_dim,
+            max_position=config.max_position_embeddings,
+            rope_parameters=config.rope_parameters[layer_type],
+        )
+        # `sliding_window` is an inclusive radius; vLLM's window counts the
+        # query token, so radius r becomes r + 1.
+        sliding_window = (
+            config.sliding_window + 1 if layer_type == "sliding_attention" else None
+        )
+        self.attn = EncoderOnlyAttention(
+            num_heads=self.num_heads,
+            head_size=self.head_dim,
+            scale=self.head_dim**-0.5,
+            num_kv_heads=self.num_kv_heads,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            per_layer_sliding_window=sliding_window,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.attn",
+        )
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        qkv, _ = self.qkv_proj(hidden_states)
+        q, k, v = qkv.split([self.q_size, self.kv_size, self.kv_size], dim=-1)
+        q, k = self.rotary_emb(positions, q, k)
+        output, _ = self.o_proj(self.attn(q, k, v))
+        return output
+
+
+class UltraBertMLP(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: UltraBertConfig,
+        quant_config: QuantizationConfig | None = None,
+        prefix: str = "",
+    ):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.gate_up_proj = MergedColumnParallelLinear(
+            config.hidden_size,
+            [config.intermediate_size] * 2,
+            bias=config.mlp_bias,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.gate_up_proj",
+        )
+        self.down_proj = RowParallelLinear(
+            config.intermediate_size,
+            config.hidden_size,
+            bias=config.mlp_bias,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.down_proj",
+        )
+        self.act_fn = get_act_and_mul_fn(config.hidden_act)
+
+    def forward(self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        gate_up, _ = self.gate_up_proj(hidden_states)
+        output, _ = self.down_proj(self.act_fn(gate_up))
+        return output
+
+
+class UltraBertLayer(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: UltraBertConfig,
+        layer_id: int,
+        quant_config: QuantizationConfig | None = None,
+        prefix: str = "",
+    ):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.input_layernorm = RMSNorm(config.hidden_size, eps=config.rms_norm_eps)
+        self.self_attn = UltraBertAttention(
+            config, layer_id, quant_config=quant_config, prefix=f"{prefix}.self_attn"
+        )
+        self.post_attention_layernorm = RMSNorm(
+            config.hidden_size, eps=config.rms_norm_eps
+        )
+        self.mlp = UltraBertMLP(
+            config, quant_config=quant_config, prefix=f"{prefix}.mlp"
+        )
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        hidden_states = hidden_states + self.self_attn(
+            positions, self.input_layernorm(hidden_states)
+        )
+        return hidden_states + self.mlp(self.post_attention_layernorm(hidden_states))
+
+
+@support_torch_compile
+class UltraBertModel(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, *, vllm_config: VllmConfig, prefix: str = ""):
+        super().__init__()
+        config: UltraBertConfig = vllm_config.model_config.hf_config
+        quant_config = vllm_config.quant_config
+
+        self.embed_tokens = VocabParallelEmbedding(
+            config.vocab_size, config.hidden_size
+        )
+        self.layers = nn.ModuleList(
+            [
+                UltraBertLayer(
+                    config,
+                    layer_id,
+                    quant_config=quant_config,
+                    prefix=f"{prefix}.layers.{layer_id}",
+                )
+                for layer_id in range(config.num_hidden_layers)
+            ]
+        )
+        self.norm = RMSNorm(config.hidden_size, eps=config.rms_norm_eps)
+
+    def embed_input_ids(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.embed_tokens(input_ids)
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        input_ids: torch.Tensor | None,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        intermediate_tensors: IntermediateTensors | None = None,
+        inputs_embeds: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        # UltraBERT feeds token embeddings to its first layer unnormalized.
+        if inputs_embeds is None:
+            inputs_embeds = self.embed_tokens(input_ids)
+        hidden_states = inputs_embeds
+        for layer in self.layers:
+            hidden_states = layer(positions, hidden_states)
+        return self.norm(hidden_states)
+
+    def load_weights(self, weights: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> set[str]:
+        stacked_params_mapping = [
+            ("qkv_proj", "q_proj", "q"),
+            ("qkv_proj", "k_proj", "k"),
+            ("qkv_proj", "v_proj", "v"),
+            ("gate_up_proj", "gate_proj", 0),
+            ("gate_up_proj", "up_proj", 1),
+        ]
+        params_dict = dict(self.named_parameters())
+        loaded_params: set[str] = set()
+        for name, loaded_weight in weights:
+            for param_name, weight_name, shard_id in stacked_params_mapping:
+                if weight_name not in name:
+                    continue
+                name = name.replace(weight_name, param_name)
+                param = params_dict[name]
+                param.weight_loader(param, loaded_weight, shard_id)
+                break
+            else:
+                param = params_dict[name]
+                weight_loader = getattr(param, "weight_loader", default_weight_loader)
+                weight_loader(param, loaded_weight)
+            loaded_params.add(name)
+        return loaded_params
+
+
+class ColUltraVBertConnector(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: ColUltraVBertConfig,
+        quant_config: QuantizationConfig | None = None,
+        prefix: str = "",
+    ):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.factor = config.pixel_shuffle_factor
+        hidden_size = config.text_config.hidden_size
+        self.modality_projection = ReplicatedLinear(
+            config.vision_config.hidden_size * self.factor**2,
+            hidden_size,
+            bias=False,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "modality_projection"),
+        )
+        self.norm = (
+            RMSNorm(hidden_size, eps=config.text_config.rms_norm_eps)
+            if config.connector_norm
+            else nn.Identity()
+        )
+
+    def pixel_shuffle(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        batch, length, dim = x.shape
+        side, f = math.isqrt(length), self.factor
+        x = x.reshape(batch, side // f, f, side // f, f, dim)
+        x = x.permute(0, 1, 3, 2, 4, 5)
+        return x.reshape(batch, length // (f * f), dim * f * f)
+
+    def forward(self, image_hidden_states: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        projected, _ = self.modality_projection(self.pixel_shuffle(image_hidden_states))
+        return self.norm(projected)
+
+
+def get_capped_longest_edge(
+    height: int, width: int, longest_edge: int, tile_size: int, max_image_tiles: int
+) -> int:
+    # Counts tiles with the tiling's own resize arithmetic, as transformers'
+    # UltraVBertImageProcessor does; a closed-form count disagrees at tile
+    # boundaries.
+    for edge in range(longest_edge, tile_size - 1, -tile_size):
+        h, w = _resize_output_size_rescale_to_max_len(height, width, max_len=edge)
+        h, w = _resize_output_size_scale_below_upper_bound(h, w, max_len=MAX_IMAGE_SIZE)
+        aspect_ratio = w / h
+        if w >= h:
+            cols = math.ceil(w / tile_size)
+            rows = math.ceil(int(cols * tile_size / aspect_ratio) / tile_size)
+        else:
+            rows = math.ceil(h / tile_size)
+            cols = math.ceil(int(rows * tile_size * aspect_ratio) / tile_size)
+        if rows * cols <= max_image_tiles:
+            return edge
+    return tile_size
+
+
+class ColUltraVBertProcessingInfo(Idefics3ProcessingInfo):
+    def get_hf_config(self) -> ColUltraVBertConfig:
+        return self.ctx.get_hf_config(ColUltraVBertConfig)
+
+    def get_image_processor(self) -> Idefics3ImageProcessor:
+        model_config = self.ctx.model_config
+        return cached_get_image_processor(
+            model_config.model,
+            revision=model_config.revision,
+            trust_remote_code=model_config.trust_remote_code,
+            processor_cls_overrides=Idefics3ImageProcessor,
+        )
+
+    def get_hf_processor(self, **kwargs: object) -> Idefics3Processor:
+        return self.ctx.init_processor(
+            Idefics3Processor,
+            image_processor=self.get_image_processor(),
+            tokenizer=self.get_tokenizer(),
+            image_seq_len=self.get_hf_config().image_seq_len,
+        )
+
+    def get_longest_edge(self, *, image_width: int, image_height: int) -> int:
+        image_processor = self.get_image_processor()
+        edge = image_processor.size["longest_edge"]
+        max_image_tiles = getattr(image_processor, "max_image_tiles", None)
+        if not max_image_tiles:
+            return edge

+            image_width,
+            edge,
+            image_processor.max_image_size["longest_edge"],
+            max_image_tiles,
+        )
+
+    def _get_image_feature_grid_size(
+        self,
+        *,
+        image_width: int,
+        image_height: int,
+        processor: Idefics3Processor,
+        mm_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],
+    ) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
+        edge = self.get_longest_edge(image_width=image_width, image_height=image_height)
+        return processor.image_processor.get_number_of_image_patches(
+            image_height, image_width, {"size": {"longest_edge": edge}}
+        )
+
+    def get_image_size_with_most_features(self) -> ImageSize:
+        processor = self.get_hf_processor()
+        edge = processor.image_processor.size["longest_edge"]
+        tile = processor.image_processor.max_image_size["longest_edge"]
+        sizes = [ImageSize(width=edge, height=h) for h in range(tile, edge + 1, tile)]
+        return max(
+            sizes,
+            key=lambda s: self.get_num_image_tokens(
+                image_width=s.width,
+                image_height=s.height,
+                processor=processor,
+                mm_kwargs={},
+            ),
+        )

+class ColUltraVBertDummyInputsBuilder(Idefics3DummyInputsBuilder):
+    info: ColUltraVBertProcessingInfo
+
+    def get_dummy_mm_data(
+        self,
+        seq_len: int,
+        mm_counts: Mapping[str, int],
+        mm_options: MultiModalDummyOptions,
+    ) -> MultiModalDataDict:
+        size = self.info.get_image_size_with_most_features()
+        return {
+            "image": self._get_dummy_images(
+                width=size.width,
+                height=size.height,
+                num_images=mm_counts.get("image", 0),
+                overrides=mm_options.get("image"),
+            )
+        }

+
+class ColUltraVBertMultiModalProcessor(Idefics3MultiModalProcessor):
+    info: ColUltraVBertProcessingInfo
+
+    def _call_hf_processor(
+        self,
+        hf_data: Mapping[str, object],
+        hf_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],
+    ) -> BatchFeature:
+        # Each image tiles at its own capped longest edge, which the HF
+        # processor only takes per call.
+        images = self.info.parse_mm_data(
+            {"image": hf_data["images"]}, validate=False
+        ).get_items("image", ImageProcessorItems)
+        outputs = []
+        for i in range(len(images)):
+            size = images.get_image_size(i)
+            edge = self.info.get_longest_edge(
+                image_width=size.width, image_height=size.height
+            )
+            outputs.append(
+                super()._call_hf_processor(
+                    {**hf_data, "images": [images.get(i)]},
+                    {**hf_kwargs, "size": {"longest_edge": edge}},
+                )
+            )
+        return BatchFeature(
+            {
+                key: torch.cat([output[key] for output in outputs], dim=1)
+                for key in ("pixel_values", "pixel_attention_mask")
+            }
+        )

+    ColUltraVBertMultiModalProcessor,

+    dummy_inputs=ColUltraVBertDummyInputsBuilder,

+    is_pooling_model = True

+    packed_modules_mapping = {
+        "qkv_proj": ["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj"],
+        "gate_up_proj": ["gate_proj", "up_proj"],

+        orig_to_new_prefix={
+            "vision_model.vision_model.": "vision_model.vision_model.",
+            "vision_model.": "vision_model.vision_model.",
+        },
+    )
+
+    def __init__(self, *, vllm_config: VllmConfig, prefix: str = ""):
+        super().__init__()
+        config: ColUltraVBertConfig = vllm_config.model_config.hf_config
+        quant_config = vllm_config.quant_config
+        self.config = config
+
+        with self._mark_tower_model(vllm_config, "image"):
+            self.vision_model = SiglipVisionModel(
+                config.vision_config,

+                prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "vision_model"),
+            )
+            self.connector = ColUltraVBertConnector(
+                config, quant_config, prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "connector")
+            )
+
+        with self._mark_language_model(vllm_config):
+            self.text_model = UltraBertModel(
+                vllm_config=vllm_config.with_hf_config(config.text_config),
+                prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "text_model"),
+            )
+
+        pooler_config = vllm_config.model_config.pooler_config
+        assert pooler_config is not None
+        self.pooler = pooler_for_token_embed(pooler_config)
+
+    def _parse_and_validate_image_input(
+        self, **kwargs: object
+    ) -> Idefics3ImagePixelInputs | None:
+        pixel_values = kwargs.pop("pixel_values", None)
+        if pixel_values is None:
+            return None
+
+        size = self.config.vision_config.image_size
+        return Idefics3ImagePixelInputs(
+            type="pixel_values",
+            pixel_values=pixel_values,
+            pixel_attention_mask=kwargs.pop("pixel_attention_mask"),
+            num_patches=kwargs.pop("num_patches"),
+            resolve_bindings={"h": size, "w": size},
+        )
+
+    def embed_multimodal(self, **kwargs: object) -> MultiModalEmbeddings:
+        image_input = self._parse_and_validate_image_input(**kwargs)
+        if image_input is None:

+
+        pixel_values = image_input["pixel_values"]
+        features = self.connector(
+            self.vision_model(pixel_values.to(dtype=self.vision_model.dtype))

+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        input_ids: torch.Tensor | None,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        intermediate_tensors: IntermediateTensors | None = None,
+        inputs_embeds: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.text_model(
+            input_ids, positions, intermediate_tensors, inputs_embeds=inputs_embeds
+        )
+
+    def load_weights(
+        self,
+        weights: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]],
+    ) -> set[str]:
+        loader = AutoWeightsLoader(self)
+        loaded = loader.load_weights(weights, mapper=self.hf_to_vllm_mapper)
+        projector = getattr(self.pooler.head, "projector", None)
+        if isinstance(projector, nn.Module):

+                f"pooler.head.projector.{name}"

+            }

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+from typing import Any
+
+from transformers import PreTrainedConfig, SiglipVisionConfig
+
+
+class UltraBertConfig(PreTrainedConfig):
+    model_type = "ultrabert"
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        vocab_size: int = 49280,
+        hidden_size: int = 768,
+        intermediate_size: int = 1024,
+        num_hidden_layers: int = 24,
+        num_attention_heads: int = 6,
+        num_key_value_heads: int | None = None,
+        head_dim: int | None = None,
+        hidden_act: str = "silu",
+        max_position_embeddings: int = 32768,
+        rms_norm_eps: float = 1e-6,
+        attention_bias: bool = False,
+        mlp_bias: bool = False,
+        sliding_window: int = 128,
+        layer_types: list[str] | None = None,
+        rope_parameters: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
+        **kwargs,
+    ):
+        if layer_types is None:
+            layer_types = [
+                "sliding_attention" if (i + 1) % 3 else "full_attention"
+                for i in range(num_hidden_layers)
+            ]
+        if rope_parameters is None:
+            rope_parameters = {
+                "sliding_attention": {"rope_type": "default", "rope_theta": 10_000.0},
+                "full_attention": {"rope_type": "default", "rope_theta": 2_560_000.0},
+            }
+
+        self.vocab_size = vocab_size
+        self.hidden_size = hidden_size
+        self.intermediate_size = intermediate_size
+        self.num_hidden_layers = num_hidden_layers
+        self.num_attention_heads = num_attention_heads
+        self.num_key_value_heads = num_key_value_heads or num_attention_heads
+        self.head_dim = head_dim or hidden_size // num_attention_heads
+        self.hidden_act = hidden_act
+        self.max_position_embeddings = max_position_embeddings
+        self.rms_norm_eps = rms_norm_eps
+        self.attention_bias = attention_bias
+        self.mlp_bias = mlp_bias
+        self.sliding_window = sliding_window
+        self.layer_types = layer_types
+        super().__init__(**kwargs)
+        # Set after the base init: transformers < 5.19 adds a shared
+        # `rope_theta` key next to the per-layer-type dicts, which 5.17 and
+        # 5.18 then reject.
+        self.rope_parameters = rope_parameters
+
+
+class ColUltraVBertConfig(PreTrainedConfig):
+    model_type = "ultravbert"
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        text_config: dict | UltraBertConfig | None = None,
+        vision_config: dict | SiglipVisionConfig | None = None,
+        image_token_id: int = 49191,
+        pixel_shuffle_factor: int = 4,
+        connector_norm: bool = True,
+        **kwargs,
+    ):
+        if not isinstance(text_config, UltraBertConfig):
+            text_config = {
+                k: v
+                for k, v in (text_config or {}).items()
+                if k not in ("model_type", "auto_map")
+            }
+            text_config = UltraBertConfig(**text_config)
+        if not isinstance(vision_config, SiglipVisionConfig):
+            vision_config = {
+                k: v for k, v in (vision_config or {}).items() if k != "model_type"
+            }
+            vision_config = SiglipVisionConfig(**vision_config)
+
+        self.text_config = text_config
+        self.vision_config: SiglipVisionConfig = vision_config
+        self.image_token_id = image_token_id
+        self.pixel_shuffle_factor = pixel_shuffle_factor
+        self.connector_norm = connector_norm
+        self.hidden_size = text_config.hidden_size
+
+        kwargs.setdefault("architectures", ["ColUltraVBertForRetrieval"])
+        super().__init__(**kwargs)
+
+    @property
+    def image_seq_len(self) -> int:
+        grid = self.vision_config.image_size // self.vision_config.patch_size
+        return grid * grid // self.pixel_shuffle_factor**2
+
+    def get_text_config(self, **kwargs):
+        return self.text_config

@@ -567,6 +567,25 @@ Supported models:
 
 Flags: `--tool-call-parser apertus`
 
+### Muse Models (`muse`)
+
+The Muse parser supports the ATEM tool-call format used by Muse Spark Open.
+Enable tool calling with `--enable-auto-tool-choice`,
+`--tool-call-parser muse`, and `--reasoning-parser muse`. `musespark1x` is an
+alias for both parsers. The `muse_glimmer` entry points share the Muse implementation while retaining
+their original channel semantics, including recipient-less tool-parser content.
+
+The parsers route `to=self` and recipient-less messages to reasoning,
+`to=user` and `to=commentary` messages to content, and tool recipients to
+ATEM tool-call extraction. `to=developer` messages are omitted. Framing
+special tokens are preserved for parsing and removed from surfaced content.
+
+The Rust frontend also provides a Muse unified parser under `muse` and
+`musespark1x`, and selects it automatically for Muse Spark model names.
+Existing automatic parser selection for Muse Glimmer is unchanged.
+
+Parser availability alone does not enable Muse Spark model execution.
+
 ### Models with Pythonic Tool Calls (`pythonic`)
 
 A growing number of models output a python list to represent tool calls instead of using JSON. This has the advantage of inherently supporting parallel tool calls and removing ambiguity around the JSON schema required for tool calls. The `pythonic` tool parser can support such models.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+"""Unit tests for the Muse ATEM tool parser and reasoning parser.
+
+Muse writes every turn as a sequence of channel-scoped messages rather
+than JSON, so the two parsers are tested together: the reasoning parser strips
+the reasoning span and forwards the remaining channels as content, and the tool
+parser reads ATEM markup out of those channels.
+
+Five areas, in order:
+
+  1. non-streaming tool-call extraction, including channel scoping (an
+     ``<atem:invoke>`` echoed inside reasoning must never become a call);
+  2. the reasoning -> tool-parser handoff, which regressed once by returning
+     ``content=None`` and starving the tool parser;
+  3. channel routing: ``to=commentary`` is content, a recipient-less
+     ``<|message|>`` is reasoning, ``to=developer`` is dropped, and a tool
+     header written without the closing ``<|eom|>`` still ends the reasoning;
+  4. streaming, where markers routinely straddle chunk boundaries, plus
+     truncation isolation for an unterminated ``to=self`` block;
+  5. tool-name normalization against the tools registered on the request.
+
+These drive the parsers directly and need no checkpoint. The tests that require
+a real tokenizer live in ``test_muse_parse_delta.py``.
+"""
+
+import json
+from contextlib import suppress
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from typing import cast
+
+import pytest
+
+from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest
+from vllm.entrypoints.openai.responses.protocol import ResponsesRequest
+from vllm.reasoning.muse_reasoning_parser import MuseReasoningParser
+from vllm.tool_parsers.muse_glimmer_tool_parser import MuseGlimmerToolParser
+from vllm.tool_parsers.muse_tool_parser import MuseToolParser
+
+R: MuseReasoningParser
+T: MuseToolParser
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def _fresh_parsers():
+    """Give each test request-scoped parser state through the real constructors."""
+    global R, T
+    R = MuseReasoningParser(object())
+    T = MuseToolParser(object())
+
+
+# Any framing token that must NEVER appear in surfaced reasoning/content.
+_FRAMING = [
+    "<|start|>",
+    "<|message|>",
+    "<|eom|>",
+    "<|eot|>",
+    "to=self",
+    "to=user",
+    "to=read.read",
+    "<atem:",
+]
+
+
+class _FakeReq:
+    """Minimal ChatCompletionRequest stand-in (no registered tools)."""
+
+    tools = None
+
+
+def _fake_req() -> ChatCompletionRequest:
+    return cast(ChatCompletionRequest, _FakeReq())
+
+
+# The parsers accept a missing request at runtime.

+
+
+def _req(*names: str) -> ChatCompletionRequest:
+    """A request with ``names`` registered as tools."""
+    return cast(
+        ChatCompletionRequest,
+        SimpleNamespace(
+            tools=[SimpleNamespace(function=SimpleNamespace(name=n)) for n in names]
+        ),
+    )
+
+
+def _call(name):
+    """One tool-call turn invoking ``name``."""
+    return (
+        f"<|start|>assistant to={name}<|message|>"
+        f'<atem:function_calls>\n<atem:invoke name="{name}">\n'
+        f'<atem:parameter name="city">Paris</atem:parameter>\n'
+        f"</atem:invoke>\n</atem:function_calls>"
+    )
+
+

+    raw = (
+        "to=self<|message|>Let me check the weather.<|eom|>"
+        "<|start|>assistant to=weather.get<|message|>"
+        '<atem:function_calls>\n<atem:invoke name="weather.get">\n'
+        '<atem:parameter name="city">Paris</atem:parameter>\n'
+        '<atem:parameter name="units">celsius</atem:parameter>\n'
+        "</atem:invoke>\n</atem:function_calls><|eot|>"

+    assert json.loads(out.tool_calls[0].function.arguments) == {

+        "units": "celsius",

+

+        '<atem:function_calls>\n<atem:invoke name="math.add">\n'
+        '<atem:parameter name="a">1</atem:parameter>\n'
+        '<atem:parameter name="b">2</atem:parameter>\n'
+        "</atem:invoke>\n</atem:function_calls><|eom|>"
+        "<|start|>assistant to=math.mul<|message|>"
+        '<atem:function_calls>\n<atem:invoke name="math.mul">\n'
+        '<atem:parameter name="a">3</atem:parameter>\n'
+        '<atem:parameter name="b">4</atem:parameter>\n'

+        delta = cur[len(prev) :]

+            R, prev, cur, delta, [], [], []
+        )
+        if dm is not None:

+            content_delta = getattr(dm, "content", None)
+            # Tool-channel content is an internal handoff to the tool parser,

+"""parse_delta-level regression tests for the Muse parsers.
+
+These drive the UNIFIED parser-engine streaming API the serving layer actually
+uses (``DelegatingParser.parse_delta``), NOT the ``extract_*_streaming`` methods
+directly. This is the coverage that was missing when a live no-tools streaming
+request leaked raw harmony framing into ``content``: the phase machine marked
+``reasoning_ended=True`` at the prompt boundary (because ``is_reasoning_end`` on
+a prompt with no ``to=self`` wrongly returned True), skipping the reasoning
+phase for the whole generation.
+
+Requires a real Muse tokenizer; skipped if the checkpoint is unavailable.
+"""
+
+import json
+import os
+
+import pytest
+
+CKPT = os.environ.get("MUSE_CKPT", "")
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not os.path.isdir(CKPT), reason=f"Muse checkpoint not found at {CKPT}"
+)
+
+_FRAMING = [
+    "<|start|>",
+    "<|message|>",
+    "<|eom|>",
+    "<|eot|>",
+    "to=self",
+    "to=user",
+    "<atem:",
+]
+
+PROMPT = "<|start|>user<|message|>hi<|eom|><|start|>assistant"
+
+
+class _Req:
+    tools = None
+    tool_choice = None
+    include_reasoning = True
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def tok():
+    from transformers import AutoTokenizer
+
+    return AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(CKPT, trust_remote_code=True)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def parser_cls():
+    from vllm.parser import ParserManager
+
+    return ParserManager.get_parser(
+        tool_parser_name="muse",
+        reasoning_parser_name="muse",
+        enable_auto_tools=True,
+    )
+
+
+def _drive(parser_cls, tok, gen_text, req=None, chunk=1):
+    """Feed gen_text token-by-token through parse_delta (as serving does)."""
+    from vllm.parser.abstract_parser import StreamState
+
+    if req is None:
+        req = _Req()
+    parser = parser_cls(tok)
+    parser._stream_state = StreamState()
+    prompt_ids = tok.encode(PROMPT, add_special_tokens=False)
+    gen_ids = tok.encode(gen_text, add_special_tokens=False)
+    reasoning, content, tools = [], [], []
+    for i in range(0, len(gen_ids), chunk):
+        delta_ids = gen_ids[i : i + chunk]
+        dm = parser.parse_delta(
+            tok.decode(delta_ids),
+            delta_ids,
+            req,
+            prompt_token_ids=prompt_ids if i == 0 else None,
+            finished=(i + chunk >= len(gen_ids)),
+        )
+        if dm is None:
+            continue
+        if getattr(dm, "reasoning", None):
+            reasoning.append(dm.reasoning)
+        if getattr(dm, "content", None):
+            content.append(dm.content)
+        for tc in getattr(dm, "tool_calls", None) or []:
+            fn = tc.function
+            name = fn.get("name") if isinstance(fn, dict) else getattr(fn, "name", None)
+            args = (
+                fn.get("arguments")
+                if isinstance(fn, dict)
+                else getattr(fn, "arguments", None)
+            )
+            tools.append((tc.index, name, args))
+    return "".join(reasoning), "".join(content), tools
+
+
+def _assert_no_framing(text):
+    for f in _FRAMING:
+        assert f not in text, f"framing {f!r} leaked: {text!r}"

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Reasoning-content parser for Muse.
+Port of the ``reasoning_content`` rule from the HuggingFace Muse
+``MUSE_GLIMMER_RESPONSE_SCHEMA`` (synced with internal master). Muse emits
+chain-of-thought in ``to=self`` channels delimited by ``<|message|>`` ... ``<|eom|>``:
+    to=self<|message|>...reasoning...<|eom|>
+Spark also routes recipient-less messages to reasoning, commentary to content,
+and drops developer messages. The Glimmer compatibility profile retains its
+original channel semantics.
+Because Muse's framing markers (``<|message|>``, ``<|eom|>``) are not guaranteed
+to be single vocab tokens across every checkpoint's tokenizer, this parser works
+on the decoded text with regexes rather than the single start/end-token base class.
+Usage: ``--reasoning-parser muse``
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator, Sequence
+
+import regex as re
+
+from vllm.entrypoints.generate.base.protocol import DeltaMessage
+from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest
+from vllm.entrypoints.openai.responses.protocol import ResponsesRequest
+from vllm.reasoning.abs_reasoning_parsers import ReasoningParser
+
+_EOM = "<|eom|>"
+_EOT = "<|eot|>"
+_FUNCTION_CALLS_OPEN = "<atem:function_calls>"
+_REASONING_OPEN = "to=self<|message|>"
+_ASSISTANT_TURN_OPEN = "<|start|>assistant"
+# A channel header: ``to=<recipient><|message|>`` where recipient is ``self``
+# (reasoning), ``user`` (final answer) or ``<tool>[.<fn>]`` (tool call).
+_CHANNEL_HEADER_RE = re.compile(r"to=(?P<recipient>[^\s<]+)<\|message\|>")
+_HEADER_PAT = r"to=[^\s<]+<\|message\|>"
+# Collapse the gap between reasoning blocks so multiple to=self spans join.
+_COLLAPSE_RE = re.compile(
+    r"<\|eom\|>(?:(?!to=self<\|message\|>).)*?to=self<\|message\|>", re.DOTALL
+)
+_REASONING_RE = re.compile(r"to=self<\|message\|>(.*?)<\|eom\|>", re.DOTALL)
+_CONTENT_RE = re.compile(
+    r"to=user<\|message\|>(.*?)(?=<\|eot\|>|<\|eom\|>|$)", re.DOTALL
+)
+# Strip a CLOSED reasoning span (header .. <|eom|>).
+_STRIP_REASONING_RE = re.compile(
+    r"(?:<\|start\|>assistant\s*)?to=self<\|message\|>.*?<\|eom\|>", re.DOTALL
+)
+# An UNTERMINATED trailing reasoning span. The model sometimes leaves the
+# analysis channel WITHOUT emitting <|eom|>, writing a bare
+# ``to=<tool><|message|>`` header instead (observed deterministically for a call
+# with EMPTY arguments on a tool that has optional parameters; reproduced on
+# other engines too, so it is a model-side defect, not engine-specific).
+#

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""ATEM tool-call parser for Muse (Muse Spark and Muse Glimmer).
+
+Port of the ``response_schema`` tool-call contract from the HuggingFace Muse
+Glimmer export (``convert_muse_glimmer_weights_to_hf.py``:
+``MUSE_GLIMMER_RESPONSE_SCHEMA``), which Muse Spark shares.
+
+Muse emits tool calls in an XML-ish ATEM format inside channel-scoped messages:
+
+    <|start|>assistant to=self<|message|>...reasoning...<|eom|>
+    <|start|>assistant to=<tool>.<fn><|message|>
+        <atem:function_calls>
+        <atem:invoke name="tool.fn">
+        <atem:parameter name="arg">value</atem:parameter>
+        </atem:invoke>
+        </atem:function_calls><|eom|>            # non-final call
+    <|start|>assistant to=user<|message|>...final answer...<|eot|>
+
+``to=commentary`` messages are user-visible updates between tool calls, and
+like ``to=user`` messages they are content; ``to=developer`` messages are
+dropped. Channel scoping is essential: an ``<atem:invoke>`` echoed inside a
+``to=self`` reasoning block or a ``to=user`` final answer must NOT be parsed as
+a real tool call.
+
+Rather than *subtracting* reasoning/answer spans with regex substitutions (the
+approach the HF ``response_schema`` uses, which is safe only on a complete,
+well-formed turn), this parser *segments* the output into messages and then
+*selects* the tool-channel bodies. On a complete turn the two are equivalent;
+on a truncated or damaged turn, subtraction can delete a valid tool call
+(an unterminated ``to=self`` block makes the non-greedy strip run to the next
+``<|eom|>``, which belongs to the tool-call message) whereas selection cannot.
+
+Usage: ``--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser muse``
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+from collections.abc import Iterator, Sequence
+
+import regex as re
+from openai.types.responses import ToolChoiceCustom, ToolChoiceFunction
+from transformers import PreTrainedTokenizerBase
+
+from vllm.entrypoints.generate.base.protocol import (
+    DeltaFunctionCall,
+    DeltaMessage,
+    DeltaToolCall,
+    ExtractedToolCallInformation,
+    FunctionCall,
+    ToolCall,
+)
+from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import (
+    ChatCompletionNamedToolChoiceParam,
+    ChatCompletionRequest,
+)
+from vllm.entrypoints.openai.responses.protocol import ResponsesRequest
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.renderers.chat_utils import make_tool_call_id
+from vllm.tool_parsers.abstract_tool_parser import (
+    Tool,
+    ToolParser,
+)
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+# --- Message framing -------------------------------------------------------
+# An assistant message header. All three parts are optional except the
+# <|message|> terminator:
+#   "<|start|>assistant to=get_weather<|message|>"  -- after an <|eom|> boundary
+#   " to=self<|message|>"                           -- first message of a turn
+#                                                      (the prompt already ended
+#                                                      with "<|start|>assistant")
+#   "<|message|>"                                   -- bare recipient (CoT,
+#                                                      treated as reasoning)
+_MSG_HEADER_RE = re.compile(
+    r"(?:<\|start\|>\s*assistant)?[^\S\n]*(?:to=(?P<rcpt>[A-Za-z0-9_.\-]+))?<\|message\|>"
+)
+_MSG_END_RE = re.compile(r"<\|eom\|>|<\|eot\|>")
+
+# Structural markers that must never reach the client. A streamed body is held
+# back by up to len(marker)-1 characters so a marker split across two chunks is
+# not emitted as content.
+_STRUCTURAL_MARKERS = ("<|eom|>", "<|eot|>", "<|start|>", "<|message|>")
+_MAX_MARKER_LEN = max(len(m) for m in _STRUCTURAL_MARKERS)
+# A trailing " to=NAME" that could still grow into a bare message header (the
+# first message of a turn has no <|start|> prefix -- the prompt ends with
+# "<|start|>assistant", so the model's first emitted text is " to=self<|message|>").
+_OPEN_TAIL_TO_RE = re.compile(r"[^\S\n]+to=[A-Za-z0-9_.\-]*$")
+
+# --- Tool-call extraction (unchanged from MUSE_GLIMMER_RESPONSE_SCHEMA) -------------
+_INVOKE_RE = re.compile(r"(<atem:invoke\b.*?</atem:invoke>)", re.DOTALL)
+_NAME_RE = re.compile(r'<atem:invoke\b[^>]*?\bname="([^"]+)"')
+_PARAM_RE = re.compile(
+    r'<atem:parameter\b[^>]*?\bname="(?P<key>[^"]+)"[^>]*?>(?P<value>.*?)</atem:parameter>',
+    re.DOTALL,
+)
+_FUNCTION_CALLS_OPEN = "<atem:function_calls>"

+def _decode_value(raw: str):
+    """JSON-decode a parameter value when possible, else keep the raw string.
+
+    Mirrors the schema's ``x-parser: json`` with ``allow_non_json: True``.
+    """
+    try:
+        return json.loads(raw)
+    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
+        return raw
+
+
+def _iter_messages(text: str) -> Iterator[tuple[str | None, str, bool]]:
+    """Segment *text* into assistant messages.
+
+    Yields ``(recipient, body, closed)`` per message, where ``recipient`` is
+    ``None`` for a bare ``<|message|>`` header and ``closed`` is False for a
+    message that has not (yet) seen ``<|eom|>`` / ``<|eot|>``.
+
+    A message is also terminated by the start of the NEXT header. Without that,
+    a reasoning block whose ``<|eom|>`` is missing (truncation, or a chunk
+    dropped at the reasoning -> tool transition) would absorb the tool-call
+    message that follows it and the call would be lost -- the same defect the
+    subtractive regexes have.
+    """
+    pos = 0
+    while pos < len(text):
+        header = _MSG_HEADER_RE.search(text, pos)
+        if header is None:
+            return
+        body_start = header.end()
+        end = _MSG_END_RE.search(text, body_start)
+        nxt = _MSG_HEADER_RE.search(text, body_start)
+        body_end = end.start() if end is not None else len(text)
+        closed = end is not None
+        if nxt is not None and nxt.start() < body_end:
+            body_end = nxt.start()
+            closed = False
+            next_pos = nxt.start()
+        else:
+            next_pos = end.end() if end is not None else len(text)
+        body = text[body_start:body_end]
+        # A body can never legitimately contain <|start|>. Seeing one means the
+        # next header is only partially generated (its <|message|> has not
+        # arrived), so the regex above could not recognise it yet. Cut there,
+        # otherwise the streamed body would grow to include the next header and
+        # then shrink back once it completes.
+        start_tok = body.find("<|start|>")
+        if start_tok != -1:
+            body = body[:start_tok]
+            closed = False
+        yield header.group("rcpt"), body, closed
+        pos = next_pos
+
+
+def _trailing_partial_marker_len(text: str) -> int:
+    """Length of the longest suffix of *text* that prefixes a structural marker."""
+    max_overlap = min(len(text), _MAX_MARKER_LEN - 1)
+    for overlap in range(max_overlap, 0, -1):
+        suffix = text[-overlap:]
+        if any(marker.startswith(suffix) for marker in _STRUCTURAL_MARKERS):
+            return overlap
+    return 0
+
+
+def _safe_open_body(body: str) -> str:
+    """Trim the tail of a still-growing body to what is safe to emit now.
+
+    Holds back anything that could still turn out to be structural, so the
+    emitted prefix only ever grows. Chunks under speculative decoding are large
+    enough that markers routinely straddle them.
+    """
+    tail_to = _OPEN_TAIL_TO_RE.search(body)
+    if tail_to is not None:
+        return body[: tail_to.start()]
+    partial = _trailing_partial_marker_len(body)
+    return body[: len(body) - partial] if partial else body
+
